articles.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
articles.summary: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption. There’s a common fear among people who work in Silicon Valley: snag one of the fast-growing, high-paying jobs in artificial intelligence, or get trapped in the “permanent underclass”, a…
body: The phrase usually describes a future in which AI automates human jobs. But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

“A lot of people say: ‘Oh, AI is lowering barriers, it’s equalizing the playing field for women,’” said Urvashi Batra, co-founder and CEO of Prioriwise, an AI platform for IT service providers. “I actually think it’s the opposite.”

Batra said people take her less seriously as the founder of an AI company than her male co-founder. When pitching investors, she and her co-founder have learned that they are more likely to get an investment if he does the pitching.

Women made up only about a quarter of new hires in AI roles in the last year, compared with 50% of new hires in non-AI roles, according to a recent report from LinkedIn. In executive roles, that number drops to just 13%. At the same time, LinkedIn’s research shows that women are more likely to work in roles with high exposure to AI disruption, like customer service, meaning they are also at higher risk for job loss due to AI.
points: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption.
But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

articles.title: 7 Fascinating Facts I Learned From an NYC Gilded Age Walking Tour
articles.summary: Keith Taillon takes a Vogue writer on a Gilded Age tour of Manhattan, stopping at iconic buildings and streets that tell the history of this iconic era.
body: On November 1, season four of The Gilded Age will premiere, and all over again, audiences will daydream about residing in ornate Beaux-Arts mansions along Fifth Avenue. While several structures from this era still stand and are open to the public—including the Frick, Cooper Hewitt, and the Morgan Library—there’s something about tracing this era of Manhattan on foot, neighborhood by neighborhood, past rows and rows of private homes, that really feels like traveling back in time. On a recent afternoon, I met up with historian Keith Taillon to do just this: view the city with fresh eyes, but through a nostalgic lens.

In addition to being a historian, author, and tour guide, Keith also runs a popular Instagram account (@ keithyorkcity ), where he rabbit holes on topics like the demolition of the original Penn Station, why we call it ‘The Big Apple,’ and Gilded Age fun facts galore. He holds a bachelor’s degree in history and a master’s in urban planning, so his tours contextualize the city’s past through its “structural configuration,” as he puts it.

articles.summary: Across the globe, hotels and resorts are building reformer Pilates studios, catering to a growing class of converts who refuse to forgo their toe taps on a red spring—even while on vacation.
body: As movement trends sweep the internet, promising shredded bodies that are then torn apart by the same online denizens who championed them months earlier, Reformer Pilates remains one of the most talked-about and booked workouts of the moment, inspiring both fervent devotion and online discourse. What was once considered a niche practice has evolved into a sought-after hospitality amenity, reflecting the growing expectations among wellness-minded travelers. For Vuori-clad devotees, no amount of “hot girl walks” on the treadmill or Teasers on the mat is going to cut it.

While there’s no shortage of reformer Pilates studios in cities like Los Angeles and New York, hotels wise to the growing demand are making themselves all the more valuable to guests by bringing the workout in-house—an ideal way to start the day before a complimentary buffet breakfast stocked with fruit and freshly pressed juices.

articles.title: A New Generation of Pakistani-American Restaurants Is Forging Its Own Path
articles.summary: From hot dogs topped with bhel puri to tikka-smothered halal hot chicken sandwiches, chefs are blending Pakistani flavors with the American foods and formats they grew up around.
body: In the summer of 2017, journalist and chef Pervaiz Shallwani and his wife, Laena McCarthy, hosted a hot dog cook-off for a friend’s birthday. Their contribution: a dog topped with bhel puri, a popular South Asian street food snack of crispy puffed rice, diced red onions, and tomatoes, and a mix of tangy and spicy chutneys. The combination—Chicago hot dog meets Karachi street food—was a happy accident, and the start of something larger to come.

While some Pakistani restaurants, like the wildly popular Aga's in Houston, recently logged as the busiest single-location restaurant on Uber Eats, and the beloved James Beard Award-nominated Zareen's Kitchen in Palo Alto, have expanded beyond a primarily Pakistani clientele, they have been the exception. The Pakistani community has long lived in the shadow of the far larger Indian American community, the second-largest immigrant group in the United States. But with the growth of the diaspora from 32,600 in 1980 to nearly 680,000 today, Pakistani restaurants are increasingly feeling the glow of the spotlight.
points: From hot dogs topped with bhel puri to tikka-smothered halal hot chicken sandwiches, chefs are blending Pakistani flavors with the American foods and formats they grew up around.

articles.title: Apple's Latest Mac Mini Is at Its Lowest Price Ever During the Final Hours of October Prime Day
articles.summary: Apple's smallest Mac is a favorite amongst AI enthusiasts and value-seekers alike. Despite its size, this Mac is as powerful as any other, which makes it as great an option for running AI agents as it is for handling simple macOS tasks.
body: While the "mini" isn't as affordable as it used to be— the memory crisis has certainly taken its toll —it's now cheaper than ever during the final hours of October Prime Day. If you've been thinking about picking up a Mac mini, now's the time to buy.

Apple's latest Mac mini runs the company's newest M6 chip, with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, 16GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. This processor is so new, in fact, that the company hasn't ported it over to its laptops yet. That means the M6 Mac mini will largely outperform Apple's M5 laptops, like the M5 MacBook Air and M5 MacBook Pro, at a much lower price. Why the discount? Because Apple isn't providing you with a keyboard, trackpad, or display. This is a standalone computer, and it is priced accordingly. It's a great value if you already have those peripherals on hand, but your investment does increase if you need to buy one, two, or three of those items.
